name: Blessed Prophets (عليهم السلام): Adam to Ibrahim

items.q: The first human and the first Prophet.
Adam (عليه السلام) was created from this.
The wife of Adam (عليه السلام), named in the hadith.
The one who refused to bow to Adam (عليه السلام) out of pride.
The Prophet who built the Ark.
The Prophet thrown into a fire that Allah made cool and safe.
The Prophet sent to the people of 'Ad.
The Prophet sent to Thamud, with a she-camel as a sign.
The son of Ibrahim (عليه السلام) who helped him raise the foundations of the House.
The son of Ibrahim (عليه السلام) whose birth was announced by angels to Sarah.
The nephew of Ibrahim (عليه السلام), himself a Prophet.
Ibrahim (عليه السلام) is called "Khalil Allah", meaning this.
The sons of Adam (عليه السلام) whose story is in Surah al-Ma'idah; the one killed is named this in the reports.
The bird that showed the son of Adam (عليه السلام) how to bury his brother.
The wife of Ibrahim (عليه السلام) and mother of Isma'il (عليه السلام).
items.src: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of the Prophets

items.q: The well that sprang up for Hajar and baby Isma'il (عليه السلام).
items.src: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of the Prophets

items.q: The two hills Hajar ran between, searching for water.
items.src: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of the Prophets

items.q: Ibrahim (عليه السلام) was commanded in a dream to sacrifice this son, by the most common view.
The animal sent in place of the son of Ibrahim (عليه السلام).
The festival that remembers the sacrifice of Ibrahim (عليه السلام).
Allah taught Adam (عليه السلام) these, which the angels did not know.
The tree Adam (عليه السلام) and his wife were told not to approach.
items.a: A tree in the Garden (unnamed in the Qur'an)

items.q: The words Adam (عليه السلام) received from his Lord were words of this.
The Prophet raised to "a high place", mentioned in Surah Maryam.
Nuh (عليه السلام) called his people for this many years less fifty.
The mountain where the Ark came to rest.
The surah named after Nuh (عليه السلام).
The people of Hud (عليه السلام) were destroyed by this.
The city of 'Ad "with lofty pillars", named in Surah al-Fajr (meaning).
Thamud carved their houses out of this.
Thamud were destroyed after they did this to the she-camel.
Ibrahim (عليه السلام) broke the idols and left this one.
The father of Ibrahim (عليه السلام), named in Surah al-An'am.
The king who argued with Ibrahim (عليه السلام) about giving life and death.
Ibrahim (عليه السلام) said "My Lord gives life and death", and then challenged the king to bring the sun from here (meaning).
The angels who visited Ibrahim (عليه السلام) were served this meal.
The people of Lut (عليه السلام) were destroyed by stones of this.
The family member of Lut (عليه السلام) who was not saved.
The House that Ibrahim and Isma'il (عليهما السلام) raised.
Iblis said he was better than Adam (عليه السلام) because he was made from this.
Adam (عليه السلام) is called this, meaning "father of mankind".
The Prophet who, after Adam (عليه السلام), is called the first Messenger sent to the people of earth.
Nuh (عليه السلام) was told to take into the Ark a pair of this.
The idols of Nuh's people, five named in Surah Nuh, include Wadd, Suwa', Yaghuth, Ya'uq and this.
Ibn 'Abbas (رِضْوَانُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِمَا) said those idols were named after these people of Nuh's time.
The people of Hud (عليه السلام) lived in this region, by the common view.
The surah named after the dunes where 'Ad lived.
Salih's people were destroyed by this.
The she-camel of Salih (عليه السلام) was to share this with the people by turns.
Ibrahim (عليه السلام) reasoned with his people about a star, the moon and this.
Ibrahim (عليه السلام) asked Allah to show him how He gives life to the dead, using these.
Ibrahim (عليه السلام) left our lady Hajar and Isma'il (عليه السلام) in a valley described as having no this.
Ishaq's son, also a Prophet, given as good news with him.
The town of Lut's people, named in the reports.
The Prophet who said "I am leaving for my Lord; He will guide me" (meaning).
The surah named after Ibrahim (عليه السلام).
Ibrahim (عليه السلام) is called this "nation" in Surah al-Nahl, a model of faith.
The religion of Ibrahim (عليه السلام) is described as this, turning away from falsehood.
The number of times Ibrahim (عليه السلام) said words that were not literally true, explained by scholars as allusions.
items.src: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of the Prophets

items.q: The word for the statues of Ibrahim's people in Surah al-Anbiya'.
The valley of Thamud, where our Beloved Prophet ﷺ told the army not to drink the water on the way to Tabuk.
Salih's people were given this many days before the punishment.
In Surah al-Naml, nine men of mischief plotted at night against this Prophet.
Ibrahim (عليه السلام) migrated with his wife Sarah and Lut (عليه السلام) to this land.
Our Beloved Master ﷺ said Ibrahim (عليه السلام) circumcised himself at this age (paraphrased).
The angels told Ibrahim (عليه السلام) they had been sent to the people of this Prophet.
Ibrahim (عليه السلام) argued with the angels on behalf of Lut's people; the Qur'an calls him this.
Our Beloved Prophet ﷺ saw Ibrahim (عليه السلام) on the Mi'raj in this heaven.
On the Mi'raj, Ibrahim (عليه السلام) was leaning against this.
Our Beloved Prophet ﷺ saw Idris (عليه السلام) on the Mi'raj in this heaven.
Our Beloved Master ﷺ saw Adam (عليه السلام) in this heaven.
The prayer of Ibrahim (عليه السلام) for a Messenger from among the people of Makkah is in this surah.
Ibrahim (عليه السلام) prayed for this city to be made safe.
Ibrahim (عليه السلام) was told to call people to this, and they would come on foot and on lean camels.
The first House set up for mankind to worship in, according to Surah Al 'Imran, is at this place.
Iblis asked to be given respite until this day.
The phrase Adam (عليه السلام) and Hawwa' said in repentance begins "Our Lord, we have wronged" these (meaning).
Our Beloved Prophet ﷺ said Adam (عليه السلام) was created on this day of the week.
The surah in which Nuh (عليه السلام) tells his people to seek forgiveness, and Allah will send rain.
In Surah Hud, the water came when this "boiled over".
Nuh's wife and Lut's wife are given in Surah al-Tahrim as examples of this.
The Prophet who said to his people, "Will you not fear Allah? I am a trustworthy Messenger to you" (meaning), in Surah al-Shu'ara' first.
Ibrahim (عليه السلام) asked his people whether their idols hear them, or do this for them.
Ibrahim (عليه السلام) said, "I am sick" (meaning), on the day of their festival, in this surah.
The father of Ibrahim (عليه السلام) threatened to do this to him.
Ibrahim (عليه السلام) promised his father to ask forgiveness for him until it became clear he was this.
The well of Zamzam was later dug again by this grandfather of our Beloved Master ﷺ.
The tribe that settled near Hajar and Isma'il (عليه السلام), and he married from it.
items.src: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of the Prophets

items.q: Ibrahim (عليه السلام) told Isma'il's first wife to tell him to change this.
items.src: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of the Prophets

items.q: The station where Ibrahim (عليه السلام) stood while building.
Isma'il (عليه السلام) is described in Surah Maryam as true to this.
The angels gave Ibrahim (عليه السلام) good news of a "forbearing boy", in this surah.
Lut's people were the first to commit this, as their Prophet said (meaning).
items.a: An indecency no one before them had done

items.q: The angels told Lut (عليه السلام) the punishment would come at this time.
The two Blessed Prophets (عليهم السلام) whose "suhuf" (scrolls) are named at the end of Surah al-A'la.
The son of Nuh (عليه السلام) who refused to board the Ark.
items.src: Qur'an 11:42-43; name from Tafsir al-Tabari, some reports say Yam

items.q: Adam (عليه السلام) lived to this age, according to a hadith.
The number of years between Adam and Nuh (عليهما السلام), per a report.
items.src: Sahih Ibn Hibban; to be checked

items.q: In a report of Abu Dharr (رِضْوَانُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ), four Arab Blessed Prophets (عليهم السلام) are named: Hud, Salih, Shu'ayb and this one.
items.src: Sahih Ibn Hibban; to be checked

items.q: The city Ibrahim (عليه السلام) came from, by the common view of historians.
Ibrahim (عليه السلام) was the first to receive guests, to wear these, and to see grey hair, per a report.
items.src: Muwatta' Malik (report of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib); to be checked

items.q: Our Beloved Prophet ﷺ said He ﷺ was the answer to the prayer of this Prophet.
